title: Higher Reasoning Effort Improves Reference Verifiability and Changes Reasoning Summaries in GPT-5.5
abstract: arXiv:2610.34212v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Large language models are increasingly being used in different stages of scientific knowledge production, including the suggestion of references. These models can operate at different levels of reasoning effort and provide summaries of their reasoning processes. This raises two questions: Does increasing reasoning effort improve the verifiability of generated references, and do the resulting reasoning summaries reveal how the model's behavior changes with greater effort? We examined summaries from GPT-5.5 as it generated scholarly references for 1,000 papers under paired low- and high-effort settings. Generated references were matched to external bibliographic records, and reasoning summaries were scored for four predefined features and explored for additional features discovered by GPT-5.5. translated_title: 更高的推理努力程度可提高GPT-5.5参考文献的可验证性并改变其推理摘要
translated_abstract: 大型语言模型正越来越多地被应用于科学知识生产的各个阶段，包括参考文献的推荐。这些模型可以在不同的推理努力水平下运行，并提供其推理过程的摘要。这引发了两个问题：提高推理努力是否能改善所生成参考文献的可验证性？由此产生的推理摘要能否揭示模型行为随更高努力而发生了怎样的变化？我们研究了GPT-5.5在配对的低努力与高努力设置下为1,000篇论文生成学术参考文献时的推理摘要。生成的参考文献与外部书目记录进行了匹配，推理摘要依据四个预定义特征进行评分，并通过GPT-5.5探索了其他新发现的特征。高努力使论文层面的解析器验证参考文献平均通过率从78.3%提升至84.8%，并产生了更长的推理摘要。所有四个p（摘要在此处被截断）
tldr: 提高推理努力程度可显著提升GPT-5.5所生成学术参考文献的可验证性（解析器验证通过率从78.3%升至84.8%），同时使其推理摘要变得更长并发生特征上的变化。
en_tdlr: Higher reasoning effort in GPT-5.5 improves the verifiability of generated scholarly references (resolver-verified rate rising from 78.3% to 84.8%) and produces longer, altered reasoning summaries.
